title: La casa poco a poco
desc: A Sunday, a bag of cement, and nobody charging anybody
setting: It is eight in the morning on a Sunday and four men you are related to by marriage are standing on your bit of land.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Ideay, cuñado. Trajimos los bloques. ¿Por dónde empezamos?
steps.en: Ideay, brother-in-law. We brought the blocks. Where do we start?

options.es: Por el primer cuarto. Con techo y puerta y ahí vivimos.
options.en: With the first room. With a roof and a door and we live in that.
options.feedback: One room first, live in it, and the rest can take ten years. Almost every house on the street was built exactly like this.
They will decide and it will be fine. It is your house, and having a plan for it is worth saying out loud.

options.es: Yo quería hacerla toda de una vez.
options.en: I wanted to build the whole thing at once.
options.feedback: Nobody has the money to build a whole house at once, and everybody has a house. Saying that out loud reads as showing off or as not understanding.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Venga, le enseño a mezclar. Arena, cemento y agua, pero no de un solo.
steps.en: Come here, I will show you how to mix. Sand, cement and water, but not all at once.

options.es: Enséñeme, don Beto. Yo nunca he hecho esto.
options.en: Show me, don Beto. I have never done this.
options.feedback: He is seventy-two and he has come on a Sunday to teach you. Admitting you cannot do it is the whole reason he is enjoying himself.
You do not. He will let you get it wrong once and then show you, which takes longer for everybody.
It is your house. Standing back while other men work on it for nothing is the one thing you cannot do today.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Aquí nadie cobra, cuñado. Pero a mediodía queremos comer.
steps.en: Nobody charges here, brother-in-law. But at midday we want to eat.

options.es: Ya está todo listo. Comida y cerveza a las doce.
options.en: Already sorted. Food and beer at twelve.
options.feedback: That is the payment and everybody knows it. A man who feeds the people who came is a man they will come back for next Sunday.

options.en: I will pay for lunch, of course.
options.feedback: Right idea. It sounds better as food you have arranged than as money you are handing over.

options.es: Les puedo dar algo por el día.
options.en: I can give you something for the day.
options.feedback: Offering your wife's brothers a wage for coming to help turns family into labour. Chino just told you the price and it was lunch.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: El otro domingo venimos otra vez. Vamos a ir levantando poco a poco.
steps.en: We will come again next Sunday. We will get it up bit by bit.

options.es: Poco a poco, pues. Aquí los espero.
options.en: Bit by bit, then. I will be waiting for you.
options.feedback: Poco a poco is not resignation here, it is the method. Say it back and you are agreeing to the next ten Sundays.
Warm. Thanks are slightly beside the point for something they consider ordinary.

options.en: And when do you think it will be finished?
options.feedback: It does not finish. That is why half the roofs on this street have iron rods sticking out of them, waiting for a second floor.
